Since this is the first round, there's nothing earlier to reconcile. I need to draft edits to the three documents as the report calls for, exercising judgment and quoting exact passages—starting with the buttons_pressed annotator prompt, where I'm replacing the full description text, making sure to match the current wording precisely before modifying it.

Next I work through the green_container annotation, replacing its tracking description with language about containers swapping places during each press and updating to the cube's exposed position once revealed. Then I revise the red/blue container annotation similarly, adding a chained-matching clause and cube-visibility condition, and update the picked_colors annotation to include a written JSON form alongside the existing example.

For the policy memory and decision rules, I rewrite the buttons_pressed logic so that the very first decision step (empty memory, no execution frames) maps to action A, while any step showing execution frames implies the first press already happened, routing to B even if buttons_pressed still reads 0. I also rework the fallback rule so point C is determined by chaining frame-by-frame from the cube's last known position rather than just picking the nearest container, since a swap means a different container now occupies that spot. I keep the previously refused items (the flat swap rule and "at least 1 at first step") as refused, retain the gripper-height heuristic with careful phrasing, and move on to writing out the final JSON.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: 1. If buttons_pressed is 0: A. 2. If buttons_pressed is 1: B.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: 1. If the carried-in memory is empty and this step shows no execution frames (the very first decision step, gripper out of frame): A. 2. If buttons_pressed (after this step's update) is 1: B. A is executed at the first step only; at any step that shows execution frames, A has already been done, so if buttons_pressed is still 0 or 1 answer B (the frames showing the gripper lowered onto a button with closed fingers count as the first press).

edits.modify_from: [y, x] of the container hiding the green cube. If a frame shows the green cube uncovered and no containers, write the cube's position. When containers appear, take the one standing on the carried-in green position. Then follow that container through the frames shown: match each container to the nearest container in the previous frame; during a button press two containers glide around each other and finish swapped, so after the press the green container sits where the other moving container started. Write its position in the last frame shown. If the green cube is exposed by lifting its container, write the exposed cube's position. Start with the cube position seen at the first step. e.g. [109, 126]
edits.modify_to: [y, x] of the container hiding the green cube. At the first step, with empty memory, WRITE the green cube's [y, x] from the scene. When containers first appear, take the container standing on the carried-in position. At every later step, match the carried-in position to the nearest container in the FIRST frame shown, then follow it frame to frame, each time choosing the container with the smallest displacement from the previous frame; never match the carried-in position straight to the last frame. Containers gliding around each other usually finish swapped, but trust the chain, not the assumption (one circling pass swaps them, two passes return them). Write the followed container's position in the last frame. If any frame shows the green cube itself (container lifted or 'held in the gripper'), write the cube's position in the last frame it is visible, and keep that cube position at later steps even once a container is lowered back over it. e.g. [109, 126]
